records.author: Alec Kriebel
records.title: Simple Young modules with nonprojective polynomial injective hulls
records.full_main_abstract: For every odd prime p, the Young module labelled by λ = (2p−2,1) in characteristic p is simple, whereas its corresponding polynomial injective hull I_n(λ) is nonprojective for every n≥2. At parameter q=1, this gives a negative answer to the unrestricted formulation of Miyachi’s Conjecture 7 in the 2009 Oberwolfach report. The proof combines classical representation theory with a labelled rank-truncation argument. We include explicit proofs of the local calculations and reproducible supporting checks. Historical priority remains unresolved; no firstness claim is made.
records.credit_and_claim_boundary: Classical representation-theory inputs credited to De Visscher–Donkin, Cox–Parker, Erdmann–Law and Miyachi; unresolved historical priority and all odd-prime/all-rank scope retained.

SEO.description: For every odd prime, a simple Young module has a polynomial injective hull that is nonprojective at every permitted rank, answering the broad printed Miyachi question negatively.

records.title: Binary consequences of relation-liveness automata lower bounds
records.full_main_abstract: We give explicit fixed-binary-alphabet consequences of OpenAI’s two relation-liveness lower bounds. Encoding each relation on h points by its h² adjacency bits gives a language recognized by a one-way nondeterministic automaton with Nₕ=(3h³−h)/2+2 states. Every equivalent two-way deterministic automaton, and every two-way nondeterministic automaton for its full binary complement, requires 2^{Ω(h)}=2^{Ω(Nₕ^(1/3))} states. We specify all transition rules, including an exact sh²-state pullback for an s-state binary target. The binary language rejects incomplete blocks; a fooling set proves that its one-way nondeterministic state complexity is Θ(h³). The exponential obstructions are inherited from the two upstream theorems; binary adjacency coding is established machinery.
records.credit_and_claim_boundary: OpenAI two pinned exponential engines, Sakoda–Sipser, Kapoutsis binary coding and the exact Adeogun–Kapoutsis/STACS/R816 comparisons remain complete; no independent base-theorem or linear-source exponent claim.

records.title: Rational-point undecidability for smooth projective varieties over the rational numbers
records.full_main_abstract: Combining OpenAI’s negative solution of rational Hilbert’s tenth problem with Poonen’s established effective transfer, we obtain undecidability of rational-point existence for arbitrary smooth projective geometrically integral varieties over ℚ. We specify a homogeneous-equation input promise and reconstruct the terminating contradiction algorithm. There is also no computable uniform bound on the height of one rational point in terms of the size of the presented equations. The arithmetic input is used with two explicit corrections documented here and in the accompanying verification supplement. This is a geometric consequence of that input; neither the geometric reduction nor the base undecidability theorem is claimed as a new independent solution.
